column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names my soul; BSB says me.

The Hebrew pictures the error lodging with me; BSB says it concerns me alone.

The Hebrew speaks of putting darkness on my paths; BSB describes veiling them.

The Hebrew narrates I went as an independent action; BSB says until I am gone.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly calls the constructed approach their way; BSB calls it a ramp.
The Hebrew says my acquaintances became strangers to me; BSB says they abandoned me.

The Hebrew says I called, using a completed action; BSB says I call.
The Hebrew explicitly names the sons of my belly; BSB says my own family.
The Hebrew says I rise and they speak against me; BSB says I appear and they deride me.
The Hebrew says I loved, using a completed action; BSB says I love.
The Hebrew makes my bone the subject of clinging to skin and flesh; BSB makes skin and flesh cling to bones.
The Hebrew repeats have pity on me; BSB abbreviates the second plea to have pity. It describes God’s hand touching me.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew joins an iron stylus and lead with and; BSB has on lead and or before chiseled in stone.
The Hebrew says as the last and upon dust; BSB says in the end and upon the earth.
The Hebrew has an active plural subject destroying the skin and says from my flesh; BSB uses a passive clause and in my flesh.
The Hebrew explicitly names kidneys in my bosom; BSB speaks of the heart yearning within me. The eyes’ seeing is expressed as completed.
The Hebrew says the root of the matter is found in me; BSB says it lies with him.
The Hebrew explicitly names wrath and the sword’s iniquities; BSB describes wrath bringing punishment by the sword.
